_about: How Amass compares organization names, everywhere it compares them: when the engine decides whether a newly found organization is one it already stored, when the duplicate and family lenses group organizations, and when collectors match a record to an organization. A name's key is the name folded to plain lower-case letters (accents removed), with '&' standing alone read as 'and', each of abbreviations written out, a leading governance_prefixes wrapper removed ('The Trustees of Utica University' is 'utica university') and trailing legal_forms removed ('Google Trust Services LLC' is 'google trust services'). Two names are the same when their keys are equal. They are near when their keys have the same number of words and the words pair one to one, each pair equal or, when both are at least near_min_length letters with no digits, alike by Jaro-Winkler at least near_similarity, a misspelling; at least one word must be distinctive (not one of generic_words). A name that only contains another, such as 'Apple Hospitality REIT' and 'Apple', is neither. Acronyms ('IBM') are not expanded: they need alias or identifier evidence. initials_stop_words are skipped when a name's initials are taken (SUNY for State University of New York); a domain label spells a name when the leading words written together are the label or begin it (at least five letters), or the label is their initials (at least three) or their initials followed by a last word in full (ngrid for National Grid), the leading words including a distinctive word. Add values here, not in Go code.
